answer_1.quote: Users increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) to assist with complex problems like coding, fact-checking, and organizing day-to-day tasks.
answer_1.outputs: step-by-step plans for solving multi-step math and trivia questions

answer_2.quote: we use Item Response Theory (IRT): an educational testing tool that models each test-taker's skill θj and exam item's difficulty βi - skill needed to solve item i - inferred from test-taker responses.

answer_3.quote: We also use GPT-4o as a generative RM, LLM-as-a-judge, predicting which p ∈ P helps users answer q more accurately/quickly - mirroring user pairwise comparisons (§3.2.1).

answer_4.quote: We have 126 English-speaking users from university courses and online forums use Planorama, collecting 4388 execution traces and 5584 preferences on 600 question/plan pairs.
answer_4.guideline: users pick which plan they think will help them solve q more accurately/quickly; users follow a plan and submit subanswers and final answers; attention checks are used to ensure quality.
